justification: Changes the zone filter behind every served numeric DCP control (web controls tab, conveyancing report, capacity engine, brief). A wrong keep/drop decision serves another zone's setback or silently drops the site's own.

falsifiable_check.fails_when: a zone_specific row written 'other than <code>' is kept for that zone or dropped for another; a code of any family (SP, RU, RE, IN, W, E, B, R, MU, C) is not honoured for 'X zone only' or for exclusion; a clause id such as C3.3.2 or B2.1 is read as a zone code; several excluded codes are not all excluded; a condition without the exclusion form is decided differently from its plain reading; a universal row or an empty zone is filtered; or a Strathfield dwelling type receives anything other than exactly its own zone's rear and side setbacks
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Old inline rule (main 8294fe0d) under test_served_zone_filter_gives_each_zone_only_its_own_rear_and_side_rows, multi_dwelling_housing: R2 FAIL (rear [(6, None), (6, 10)], both side sets); R3, R4, E1 FAIL (rear [], side [1.2, 2.7]). The version the push-time cross-review rejected (10-code substring list, R/E/B/MU/C-only exclusion) FAILS test_every_zone_family_is_read_for_inclusion_and_exclusion at ('SP2 zone only', 'R2') and test_clause_ids_are_not_zone_codes ('see Part B2.1' read as zone B2). The new version passes all of them. My first draft of test_conditions_without_the_exclusion_form_decide_as_before wrongly expected 'other than the R2 zone; R4 only' to exclude R2; it now pins that this is not the exclusion form. 450 tests pass across test_conveyancing_db, test_insert_strathfield_general_residential, test_dcp_controls_api, test_conveyancing_dcp_needs_review and test_constraint_arithmetic.

pre_impl.existing_data: Measured 2026-09-14 on the live database: 868 current, visible dcp_setback_controls rows, 74 of them zone_specific; codes named in zone_specific conditions are R1-R4, E1-E3, B1, B2, B4 and MU1, and none names only codes outside the old list. The only 'other than' zone_specific rows are Strathfield's five other-zones rows (1266, 1267, 1284, 1285, 1286), worded without codes, so an R2 site given its zone receives both the R2 rows and these. Old inline rule vs zone_row_applies over all 868 rows x 45 zone codes (R1-R5, E1-E5, B1-B8, MU1, C1-C4, RU1-RU6, IN1-IN4, SP1-SP5, RE1-RE2, W1-W4, and no zone): 39,060 decisions, 0 differ.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: The filter assumed a zone-specific condition only names the zones it applies to, and only ever names one of ten codes. The Strathfield General Residential DCP (C3.4.2, C3.6.1-C3.6.2) writes rules for R2 and for 'all other zones', and zones such as SP2, RU5, RE1, IN2 or W1 were invisible to the list, so a row naming only them applied everywhere (cross-review HIGH findings on #1103 and on the first push of this branch).
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: The inline predicate in fetch_dcp_setbacks becomes zone_row_applies(applicability, condition, zone_prefix): zone codes are whole tokens of any Standard Instrument family (not followed by another digit or a '.digit' clause suffix); 'other than' followed directly by codes excludes those codes; otherwise a condition naming codes applies only to those codes, and one naming none applies everywhere. fetch_dcp_setbacks calls it at the same point; the SQL, ordering, needs_review guard and output shape are unchanged. The pattern lives in conveyancing_db.py because the backend image copies only services/ and scripts/conveyancing_db.py. Strathfield's five other-zones conditions are reworded to 'zones other than R2 Low Density ...'.
pre_impl.external_source_error: The external sources are the production database behind fetch_dcp_setbacks and the zone code callers pass in (from the Planning Portal zoning lookup). A missing or blank zone still means no filtering. Legacy and current codes are not aliased by either rule: a row naming legacy B2 is dropped for a site reported as current E1, as before. A condition that mis-states its exclusion (for example 'other than the R2 zone') is read as naming R2; the tests pin that reading.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No shape change. fetch_dcp_setbacks still returns setbacks/sd_setbacks lists of dicts (type, value_min/value_max float | null, unit, clause, notes, source_text, source_chapter_key, pdf_page, dcp_version, applicability) that services/dcp_controls_api.py proxies to frontend-nextjs/app/api/dcp/structured-controls/route.ts (controls grouped by category, pdf_url string | null). Only which rows are in the lists changes, and on today's data only for rows written in the exclusion form.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: Today a Strathfield R2 multi-dwelling-housing enquiry that passes its zone sees two rear setbacks and both side setback sets, and cannot tell from the numbers which apply; a future row scoped to SP2 or RU5 would be shown to every other zone. If this change were wrong the failure would be silent in the other direction: a site's own setback missing from the controls tab, the PDF and the capacity arithmetic with nothing to say it was dropped. The per-zone Strathfield test, the family tests and the zero-difference measurement are the checks.

functions.name: zone_row_applies
functions.input: A row's applicability string or None, its condition text or None, and the site's zone code prefix such as 'R2' or 'SP2' (empty when no zone is known).
functions.output: True when the row should be served for that zone: always for non-zone_specific rows, empty zones or empty conditions; for 'other than <codes>' conditions True unless the zone is one of those codes; otherwise True when the condition names no zone code or names the site's zone.
functions.if_none: None applicability or None condition returns True, the same as the inline rule did.

functions.name: fetch_dcp_setbacks
functions.input: An open database connection, an LGA slug, an optional zone code string such as 'R2 Low Density Residential', and raise_on_error.
functions.output: The same controls dict as before; each row is now kept or dropped by zone_row_applies (scripts/conveyancing_db.py:646) instead of the inline block.
functions.if_none: A None or blank zone code still yields an empty zone prefix and no zone filtering; a None slug still returns None before any query.

real_layer_exempt.scripts/conveyancing_db.py: Measured against the real database instead of a DB-marked test: the old inline rule and zone_row_applies were evaluated for every current visible row (868) for 45 zone codes plus no zone, 39,060 decisions, 0 different (2026-09-14). fetch_dcp_setbacks itself is exercised through the existing mock-cursor TestZoneFilter plus the new exclusion, family and clause-id cases.
real_layer_exempt.scripts/insert_strathfield_general_resid: Its data change is applied to production by a guarded sync that imports ROWS, checks the pinned PDF, backs up, updates only differing conditions and requires every live Strathfield row to equal ROWS; its dry run on 2026-09-14 updated exactly rows 1266, 1267, 1284, 1285, 1286 and reported 'identical: True' before rolling back. It is applied only after this code is deployed (post_merge).

values: N/A - no stored value is read or written by the changed code; the Strathfield rows change condition text only, and that write happens after deploy (post_merge).
queries: N/A - no SQL changes; fetch_dcp_setbacks runs the same SELECT and only the per-row keep/drop decision moves into zone_row_applies.

break_it.scenario: Another council's live condition already contains a zone code the old ten-code list ignored, or 'other than' followed by a code, so its rows would suddenly be kept or dropped differently.
break_it.what_happens: Rows that sites saw yesterday could disappear or appear today without any data change.
break_it.how: Measured before committing: old rule vs zone_row_applies over all 868 live rows for 45 zone codes and no zone - 39,060 decisions, 0 differ. Only rows reworded to the exclusion form change.
break_it.repro: Evaluate both rules for every row of SELECT id, applicability, condition FROM dcp_setback_controls WHERE is_current AND NOT needs_review across the zone list

break_it.scenario: A control scoped 'SP2 Infrastructure zone only' (or RU5, RE1, IN2, W1) is fetched for an R2 site.
break_it.what_happens: The old substring list did not know SP2, so the row applied everywhere and an infrastructure-zone setback was served to a residential site.
break_it.how: Zone codes of every family are read as whole tokens; test_every_zone_family_is_read_for_inclusion_and_exclusion checks each family is kept for its own zone and dropped for another, and failed on the rejected version at ('SP2 zone only', 'R2').

break_it.scenario: A condition cites a clause or DCP part whose id looks like a zone, such as '(C3.3.2)' or 'see Part B2.1'.
break_it.what_happens: Read as zone C3 or B2, the row would be dropped for every site not in that zone.
break_it.how: A code followed by '.digit' is not a zone token; test_clause_ids_are_not_zone_codes failed on the rejected version ('Part B2.1' read as B2) and passes now.

break_it.scenario: A council author writes the exclusion as 'other than the R2 zone' instead of 'other than R2'.
break_it.what_happens: The exclusion branch does not fire and the condition reads as naming R2, so an R2 site keeps a row meant for every other zone while R3 sites lose it.
break_it.how: Not detected automatically; test_conditions_without_the_exclusion_form_decide_as_before pins the reading, the docstring states the required form, and the memory note records it for future inserts.

break_it.scenario: The Strathfield rows are reworded to 'zones other than R2 ...' while the Railway backend still runs the old inline rule.
break_it.what_happens: The old rule reads R2 as the named zone, so R3, R4 and E1 sites lose their rear and 4m/2m side setbacks and R2 sites keep them (observed under the old rule).
break_it.how: The sync is deferred until the merge commit carries Railway's 'refreshing-hope - nswcompliance: success' status; post_merge records the order.

break_it.scenario: A rule excludes several zones at once, written 'all zones other than R2, R3 and E1'.
break_it.what_happens: A parser that read only the first code would serve the rule to R3 and E1 sites it excludes.
break_it.how: The exclusion pattern accepts codes joined by commas, slashes, 'and' or 'or', and every code in the match is excluded; test_other_than_several_zones checks R4 kept, R3 and E1 dropped.

break_it.scenario: A row names legacy code B2 and the Planning Portal reports the site as current E1 (or the reverse).
break_it.what_happens: Neither the old nor the new rule aliases legacy to current codes, so the row is dropped for a site it covers.
break_it.how: Unchanged from before and stated in the docstring and external_source_error; aliasing needs the legacy->current map at runtime, which the backend image does not ship (enrichment/config is not copied).
break_it.repro: python -c "import importlib.util as u; s=u.spec_from_file_location('c','scripts/conveyancing_db.py'); m=u.module_from_spec(s); s.loader.exec_module(m); print(m.zone_row_applies('zone_specific','B2 zone only','E1'))"

break_it.scenario: The capacity engine (services/constraint_arithmetic.py) receives the now-deduplicated Strathfield rows for an R2 multi-dwelling-housing site.
break_it.what_happens: If it averaged or took the first row, removing the other-zone rows could lower the side or rear setback it computes with.
break_it.how: _get_dcp_value takes the largest value_min per control; for R2 the kept rows still include the 5m side and the 6m rear floor, so no computed setback falls. test_constraint_arithmetic passes unchanged.

break_it.scenario: The web controls tab calls the backend without a zone for a Strathfield property.
break_it.what_happens: Both the R2 rows and the other-zones rows are listed; with no zone there is nothing to choose between them.
break_it.how: By design: an empty zone prefix applies every row (test_no_zone_code_includes_all and the empty-zone assertion); each row's condition says which zone it is for.

post_merge.db_reset: Yes: after the merge commit shows Railway's 'refreshing-hope - nswcompliance: success' status, run the Strathfield sync (dry run then --apply) that rewords conditions of rows 1266, 1267, 1284, 1285, 1286 to 'zones other than R2 Low Density ...' with a backup and the ROWS equality check; then python scripts/dq_probe_live.py --id DQ-32b must print CLEAN.
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes: after the sync, the backend controls for strathfield with zone R2 must list only the 6-10m rear setback and the 5m/3m side setbacks for multi-dwelling housing, and with zone R3 only the 6m rear and 4m/2m side setbacks; with no zone, both sets with their conditions.
